bull.b: A large, growing deposit base gives Ally a durable funding platform and supports its primarily digital banking model. Deposit funding can improve liquidity and reduce reliance on wholesale sources, while customer growth broadens the franchise supporting future lending and fee opportunities.

Rising earning assets combined with expanding net interest margin can strengthen recurring net interest income, Ally’s core earnings engine. The upgraded growth outlook and stated path toward an upper-3s margin suggest improved operating earnings potential over the next several quarters.

Six consecutive quarters of improving retail auto charge-offs indicate that credit performance is becoming a more supportive earnings factor. Better loss trends can reduce provision pressure, protect capital, and improve the durability of returns as Ally expands its lending assets.

bear.b: Persistently elevated leverage reduces Ally’s financial flexibility if profitability or credit performance weakens. It can constrain capital allocation and make balance-sheet management more demanding, leaving the company with less capacity to absorb adverse lending conditions or fund growth internally.

Thin and volatile free cash flow relative to operating cash flow raises questions about the consistency of cash available after other demands. This may limit internally generated flexibility for capital returns, balance-sheet investment, or absorbing periods of higher provisions and funding costs.

Credit remains a structural earnings sensitivity because reserve builds and delinquencies can increase provisions as the loan book grows. Persistent consumer affordability concerns or weaker repayment trends could offset margin benefits, reduce earnings, and require more capital for loss absorption.
